Global Markets Brief
Dear Investor,
This week, we take a closer look at where the Indian market stands after the recent correction. As valuations reset and market dynamics continue to shift, the gap between different parts of the market is becoming more visible. We explore what has changed, where the market stands today, and what could shape its direction from here.

Equity · Valuations
India Breaks Its Support Level
Diving Back To March
Everyone is talking about the Nifty falling back towards the levels seen during the March crisis. At 22,421, the index is now only around 1% above its April low of 22,183, almost wiping out the recovery that followed the March sell-off.
The break below 23,000 has made the correction more significant. What started as a pullback from the year's high has now taken the market back to the same zone where investors were rebuilding confidence only a few months ago.
Valuations Have Fallen
At first glance, the Nifty looks cheaper. Its P/E has fallen to 19.2x, below its long-term historical median, making this a visible valuation reset rather than just a price correction. But India is still an expensive market overall. Beyond the headline index, the Nifty 500 trades around 21.8x, while the Midcap 150 and Smallcap 250 remain at much higher valuations. Parts of the market still look expensive, and there is a reason for that.
Relative Valuations
The Nifty and Sensex give us the broad picture, but underneath them sit large caps, midcaps, small caps and sector indices, each with a very different valuation and earnings profile. Comparing India with markets outside it, both globally and within EMs, makes it clear why India cannot be called cheap simply because its valuations are falling. MSCI India still trades well above MSCI EM.
Mid & Small Caps Look Interesting, But Not Cheap
Mid and small caps have a strong long-term earnings and returns record. The Smallcap 250 has delivered around 15% annualised over five years, compared with about 6% for the Nifty 50, showing how much stronger compounding has been in the broader market. But that performance has also pushed valuations higher. At around 34.5x earnings, small caps still command a large premium to large caps. That leaves less room for disappointment and keeps this a higher-risk part of the market, despite the stronger growth record.
Where The Sector Opportunity Sits
Healthcare and pharma valuations remain much higher, so the case there is less about being cheap and more about earnings visibility and structural demand. Healthcare is an attractive area to watch, but at a valuation that remains stretched. Putting sector earnings expectations alongside current valuations, Realty stands out, combining the strongest expected earnings growth with a meaningful discount to its historical average.
Earnings Are Doing Their Part
The valuation reset is not happening because earnings have disappeared. Nifty earnings have grown at roughly 12% annually over the past five years, while the index price has grown at only about 5%, bringing the P/E down from around 27x to 19x. This makes the current correction different from an earnings collapse. Prices have adjusted faster than earnings, creating a more meaningful valuation reset in large caps.
Continued Pressure On Positioning
The problem is that the wider market environment has not become easier. Oil remains elevated, global bond yields are high and the rupee is under pressure, keeping the backdrop difficult for foreign investors and making India's valuation premium harder to ignore. Foreign selling has remained a major part of the correction, even as domestic investors continue to provide support. Domestic liquidity is absorbing some of the selling, but global conditions are still setting the direction.
Why It Matters
India is now mildly undervalued, but the opportunity is not evenly spread across the market. The correction has improved the entry point, while making valuation, earnings and segment selection more important than simply taking a broad India view. The market is opening a clearer gap between areas where prices have reset and areas where valuations remain demanding.
